# Meridian Core — Data Dictionary

Generated from `spec/`. Column → API field mapping: API fields use the column name; `—` means the column is not exposed.

## Deposits and Accounts (`accounts`)

Deposit account servicing on top of the ledger: current, savings, call and notice accounts, term deposits, savings pots, sweeps, standing orders, overdrafts, holders and mandates, blocks, dormancy, closure, cheques, virtual accounts, daily interest accrual and capitalisation, fee charging, statements and tax certificates.


### Service `deposit-service` — database `accounts_db`

Owns deposit accounts and everything around them. Opens a ledger account per deposit account, drives daily interest accrual and capitalisation, fee charging, overdrafts, term deposits, pots, sweeps, standing orders, dormancy and closure. Never changes balances itself; it posts through the ledger.

## Card Issuing and Processing (`cards`)

Card issuing processor: card programs and products, virtual and physical cards, card controls, PCI card data vault, real-time ISO 8583 authorisation inside the ledger with JIT funding and stand-in, network tokenisation, 3-D Secure, clearing and settlement, interchange and fees, and scheme disputes.


### Service `card-service` — database `card_db`

Card programs, card products, card lifecycle (issue, activate, freeze, replace, close), physical card orders through bureaus, card controls and spend limits, PIN events and credit card statement cycles.

### Service `card-vault-service` — database `card_vault_db`

PCI DSS scoped card data vault. Stores PAN, CVV2 and expiry encrypted with envelope encryption under HSM-managed keys and returns tokens. Isolated network segment; only authorisation, tokenisation and reveal flows may detokenise.

### Service `card-authorization-service` — database `card_auth_db`

Real-time authorisation: receives ISO 8583 from the card gateway, applies card status, controls, limits, fraud score and 3DS outcome, places or increments the ledger hold (or calls JIT funding), and responds within the scheme budget. Runs stand-in when the ledger is unavailable.

## Customer, Agent, Business and Merchant Channels (`channels`)

Experience APIs for the bank's own apps. Customer apps (web banking, mobile) use /v1/me: every operation acts for the signed-in customer only: the customer comes from the access token (customer_id claim, scope channels:customer), never from a path, query or body. The service calls the domain services with its own service identity and the customer's tenant, checks that every referenced account, card, loan, wallet, payment, payee, standing order, thread, notification and document belongs to the customer (an object of someone else answers 404), rebuilds request bodies server-side and requires a recent authentication (step-up) for money movement and security changes. Agent outlet apps use /v1/agent the same way (agent_id claim, scope channels:agent; see agent-channel-service), the business banking portal uses /v1/business (business_customer_id and business_user_id claims, scope channels:business; see business-channel-service), and the merchant app uses /v1/merchant (merchant_id and merchant_user_id claims, scope channels:merchant; see merchant-channel-service). Domain services keep their operator APIs; customer, agent, business and merchant tokens carry no domain scope and are rejected there.


### Service `customer-channel-service` — database `customer_channel_db`

Customer channel BFF behind /v1/me. Stateless towards domain data (reads and acts through the owning services); keeps only the audit trail of what each customer did or was refused.

### Service `agent-channel-service` — database `agent_channel_db`

Agent channel BFF behind /v1/agent for the agent outlet app (offline PWA). Every operation acts for the signed-in agent only: the agent comes from the access token (agent_id claim, scope channels:agent), never from a path, query or body. Calls the domain services with its own service identity and the agent's tenant, checks that every referenced outlet, till, device, float request, cash request, transaction, bill payment, top-up, commission earning, onboarding application, document and offline batch belongs to the agent (404 otherwise, audited and published), rebuilds request bodies server-side (agent, outlet, float wallet, currency, channel) and requires a recent login or a device-bound proof for money movement. Devices register a public signing key (ES256 or Ed25519); offline batches and device proofs are verified against it. Keeps the device keys, the customer lookup log and the audit trail of what each agent did or was refused.

### Service `business-channel-service` — database `business_channel_db`

Business banking portal BFF behind /v1/business. Every operation acts for the signed-in business user only: the business (a non-individual customer of customer-service) and the user come from the access token (business_customer_id and business_user_id claims, scope channels:business), never from a path, query or body. Owns the business-user model: users and roles (ADMIN, MAKER, APPROVER, VIEWER) managed by the business admin, per-user account entitlements (view, initiate, approve, per-payment cap), the approval matrix (amount bands per currency, number of approvers, any-order or sequential approvers, self-approval never allowed) and per-user daily limits. Payments, bulk payments and payroll are drafted and approved here and released to payment-service with the service identity only after the final approval (idempotent). Calls the domain services with its own service identity and the business's tenant, checks that every referenced account, payee, payment, mandate, collection, virtual account, payment link, card, loan, credit line, FX quote, statement, API client and webhook endpoint belongs to the business (404 otherwise, audited and published), rebuilds request bodies server-side and requires a recent authentication (step-up) for approvals, money movement and administration. Loan and credit-line repayments, credit-line draws, mandates, collections, virtual accounts and payment links go through the approval matrix when a rule names their type and covers the amount (released once after the final approval), else run immediately. Machine-to-machine access: client-credentials tokens of an API client created for the business carry the business, its TECHNICAL user and the m2m marker (docs/BUSINESS_M2M_API.md). Bank staff provision a business's first ADMIN (/v1/business-provisioning, scope channels:admin).

### Service `merchant-channel-service` — database `merchant_channel_db`

Merchant app BFF behind /v1/merchant. Every operation acts for the signed-in merchant user only: the merchant (a merchant of merchant-service) and the user come from the access token (merchant_id and merchant_user_id claims, scope channels:merchant), never from a path, query or body. Owns the merchant-user model: users with roles (OWNER, MANAGER, CASHIER, VIEWER) and store scoping (OWNER and all-stores users work in every store, others only in their assigned stores), sales started from the app (one dynamic EMVCo QR per sale, issued by merchant-service, with live status), refund requests with four-eyes approval (a cashier requests, a manager or owner other than the requester approves with a recent authentication; the cumulative refunds of a payment never exceed it) and payout (settlement) account changes (owner request, approval by another owner or manager, both with step-up). Calls the domain services with its own service identity and the merchant's tenant, checks that every referenced store, terminal, sale, transaction, refund, payment link, settlement, payout account, API client and webhook endpoint belongs to the merchant and to the user's stores (404 otherwise, audited and published), and rebuilds request bodies server-side.

## Engagement: Rewards, Insights and Campaigns (`engagement`)

Customer engagement: loyalty rewards, points and cashback, referral programs, transaction enrichment and personal finance insights (PFM), targeted campaigns and personalised offers, and secure customer messaging.


### Service `rewards-service` — database `rewards_db`

Loyalty programs: earn rules on spend and behaviour, points accounts with an append-only points ledger, cashback, tiers, a redemption catalogue, and referral programs with qualification and payouts.

### Service `insights-service` — database `insights_db`

Personal finance management: transaction enrichment (clean merchant names, logos, categories, geo, recurring flags), category taxonomy and customer overrides, budgets, subscription detection, insight cards and cash-flow forecasts.

### Service `inbox-service` — database `inbox_db`

Secure, authenticated two-way messaging between customers and the bank with attachments and read receipts, plus in-app announcements and banners. Who is speaking is never taken from the request body: the caller is CUSTOMER only when an internal service token (the customer channel service) relays the call with the X-On-Behalf-Of-Customer header (customer id; ignored for any other caller, 403 when a non-internal token sends it); every other authenticated principal is bank-side (STAFF). Customer callers are confined to their own threads (404 otherwise), never see internal notes and cannot assign, edit or read the message/receipt resources; opened_by, sender_type, sender_user_id, reader_type and reader_user_id are server-set.

## Ledger and Accounting (`ledger`)

The single source of truth for money. A real-time, append-only double-entry ledger that every other service posts through, the general ledger and period close, and automated reconciliation.


### Service `ledger-service` — database `ledger_db`

Posting engine and balance service. The only component allowed to change balances. Enforces double-entry, idempotency, holds and available-balance rules; publishes every posting.


#### `ledger`

A book of accounts for one legal entity (a tenant may run several ledgers)

### Service `reconciliation-service` — database `recon_db`

Imports external statements and settlement files, matches them against internal ledger records with configurable rules (and AI suggestions), and manages breaks in ageing exception queues.

#### `recon_adjustment`

A requested ledger adjustment or write-off for a break. Four-eyes: the approver (direct or through central approvals) must differ from the requester; on approval the journal entry is posted to ledger-service and the break closes (RESOLVED for an adjustment, WRITTEN_OFF for a write-off).

## Lending and Collections (`lending`)

Loan origination with bureau, scoring and explainable decisions; loan servicing for instalment loans, revolving credit lines, BNPL and nano-loans; collateral management; and collections and recovery.


### Service `loan-origination-service` — database `loan_origination_db`

Loan and credit-line applications from any channel: applicants, declared finances, documents, credit bureau pulls, scorecards with explainable reason codes, affordability, decisions, offers and e-signature.

### Service `loan-service` — database `loan_db`

Loan and credit-line servicing: disbursement, schedules, daily accrual, repayment allocation waterfall, fees, rate changes, restructuring, prepayment, delinquency (DPD) tracking, write-off and recovery. All money movements are posted through ledger-service.

### Service `collections-service` — database `collections_db`

Collections and recovery for loans, credit lines, cards, overdrafts and BNPL: strategies by segment and DPD, automated contact actions, agent queues, promises to pay, payment plans, AI next-best-action and legal proceedings.

## Open Banking (`openbanking`)

Regulated third-party access (ASPSP side). Registers and certifies TPPs, manages AIS / PIS / CBPII / VRP consents and their SCA authorisation, logs every data access, and exposes standard profiles (UK OBIE, Berlin Group NextGenPSD2, Brazil Open Finance, FDX, CDR) mapped onto Meridian core APIs.


### Service `openbanking-service` — database `openbanking_db`

ASPSP open banking gateway. Validates TPP identity (eIDAS / directory certificates), manages consents and SCA redirect / decoupled flows, enforces consent scope on every call, and translates standard profiles to internal account, payment and funds-check APIs.

## Operations: Batch, Files, Search and Archive (`operations`)

Business-day processing and EOD/EOM/EOY batch orchestration, secure file exchange with partners, enterprise search across all entities, and data retention, archival, legal hold and certified purge.


### Service `business-day-service` — database `business_day_db`

Owns the business date per legal entity, orchestrates EOD/EOM/EOQ/EOY job graphs with dependencies, parallelism, retries and restart-from-failure, performs the date roll, and schedules non-EOD batch jobs with distributed locks. Jobs execute in the owning services; this service coordinates them (Temporal).

#### `eod_job_definition`

A step in an end-of-period job graph, executed by an owning service. Cross-service EOD contract: for every tenant, EOD run, job and partition the orchestrator calls <http_method> <owning_service><http_path> with headers X-Tenant-Id (the tenant whose EOD runs) and Idempotency-Key = "eod:<eod_run_id>:<job code>:<partition_no>" (identical for every retry of the partition, so a lost response is executed once downstream). Placeholders {business_date}, {legal_entity_id}, {cycle_type}, {eod_run_id}, {eod_job_run_id}, {job_code}, {partition_no}, {partition_count} and {attempt} are substituted (URL-encoded) in http_path and in the string values of body_template. Without body_template the body is the job context (eod_run_id, eod_job_run_id, job_code, job_type, cycle_type, legal_entity_id, business_date, is_month_end, is_quarter_end, is_year_end, partition_no, partition_count, partition_key, attempt, parameters, checkpoint). Example: deposit-service POST /v1/deposit-accounts/eod/accrue?business_date={business_date}. The job answers 2xx with optional records_processed, records_failed and checkpoint; 408, 409, 429 and 5xx are retried per the failure policy, other 4xx fail the job.

#### `eod_trigger_policy`

When end-of-day starts automatically for a legal entity. The platform scheduler (cross-tenant EOD trigger) starts EOD for the current business date once the local cut-off time has passed in the policy's time zone (default: the legal entity's, else the tenant's time zone). One policy per legal entity plus an optional tenant default (empty legal_entity_id); without any policy the platform default cut-off applies.

#### `eod_sweep`

One execution of the platform's cross-tenant EOD trigger: lists the ACTIVE tenants from tenant-service and, per tenant and legal entity whose business date is due, starts EOD under that tenant (idempotent per tenant, legal entity and business date: a date with an EOD run is never started again). Platform-global record.

### Service `file-gateway-service` — database `file_gateway_db`

Managed file transfer with banks, schemes, bureaus, regulators and partners over SFTP, FTPS, S3, AS2 and APIs: PGP encryption, virus scanning, format validation, routing of inbound files to consumer services, generation and delivery of outbound files, acknowledgements and a complete transfer audit trail.

### Service `search-service` — database `search_db`

Enterprise search across customers, accounts, wallets, cards, loans, payments and cases. Maintains OpenSearch indices fed by domain events (CDC), with versioned mappings, zero-downtime reindexing via alias swaps, synonyms, field-level masking by role, and saved searches per user.

### Service `archive-service` — database `archive_db`

Data lifecycle management: data classification catalogue, retention policies per data class and jurisdiction, archival of aged records to immutable object storage with manifests, legal holds that override retention, anonymisation, and approved purges with certificates of destruction.

## Customer and Onboarding (`party`)

Single customer view for individuals and businesses (CIF), relationships and UBOs, tiered KYC, devices and credentials, consent and privacy, configurable onboarding journeys, and KYC/KYB checks through pluggable providers.


### Service `customer-service` — database `customer_db`

Customer information file (CIF): individuals and businesses, identifiers, addresses, contacts, relationships and UBOs, groups and households, segments, KYC tier, devices, credentials, consent and privacy requests. Provides the single customer view across all products.


#### `customer`

### Service `onboarding-service` — database `onboarding_db`

No-code onboarding journeys per product, segment and country; runs applications step by step across app, web, USSD, agent and branch channels, orchestrates KYC checks and decisions, and syncs offline agent-assisted applications. Unauthenticated prospects use the public applicant surface (/v1/onboarding/public/applications): start on a published journey by code (rate-limited, attestation token), then act with a short-lived opaque applicant token sent as X-Applicant-Token, stored only as a SHA-256 hash and bound to one application (any other application answers 404), rotated through token/refresh.

### Service `kyc-service` — database `kyc_db`

KYC/KYB orchestration: document capture and OCR, liveness and face match, database and registry checks, UBO discovery, PEP/sanctions/adverse-media screening at onboarding, risk rating with factors, periodic review and document-expiry refresh, all through pluggable providers.

## Payments Hub (`payments`)

ISO 20022-native payments hub. Initiates, screens, approves, routes, submits and settles payments on every rail (instant, batch, RTGS, mobile money, cross-border); manages payees, aliases, bulk files, direct-debit mandates, request-to-pay, payment links and QR codes; runs rail routing, settlement, liquidity and FX.


### Service `payment-service` — database `payment_db`

Payment orchestrator. Owns the payment lifecycle state machine (initiate, screen, approve, hold funds, route, submit, settle, return), payees and aliases, bulk payments, mandates, collections, request-to-pay, payment links and QR codes. Runs multi-step flows as Temporal sagas with compensations.

## Platform and Administration (`platform`)

Cross-cutting platform capabilities: multi-tenancy and cells, legal entities and branches, staff identity and access (RBAC + ABAC, SSO, MFA), API clients and keys, versioned configuration and country packs, reference data, documents and e-signature, maker-checker approvals and workflows, notifications, webhooks, the tamper-evident audit log, and SaaS usage metering and billing.


### Service `tenant-service` — database `tenant_db`

Tenant lifecycle and placement on cells, legal entities, branches, per-tenant settings, feature flags, enabled modules and white-label branding.

### Service `webhook-service` — database `webhook_db`

Delivers domain events to client endpoints: signed (HMAC-SHA256 + timestamp), at-least-once with exponential retries for 72 hours, ordering per aggregate, delivery logs and event replay.

## Product Studio and Pricing (`product`)

Versioned, configuration-driven product catalogue for every product family (deposits, wallets, cards, loans, lines, BNPL, overdrafts), with interest, fees, tax, limits, eligibility, bundles, sandboxed WASM scripts and simulation; plus a DMN-compatible pricing and decision engine.


### Service `product-catalog-service` — database `product_db`

Product Studio back end. Holds templates, products and immutable published versions with all parameters (interest, fees, tax, limits, eligibility, scripts). Accounts pin a version; publishing goes through maker-checker; simulations run a product against synthetic customers.

### Service `pricing-rules-service` — database `pricing_db`

DMN-compatible decision engine used for pricing, eligibility, fees, limits and routing decisions. Decision tables are versioned with maker-checker; every evaluation is logged for explainability.

## Regulatory Reporting, Analytics and AI (`reporting`)

Country-pack regulatory reporting (definitions, runs, validation, submission, CRS/FATCA), self-service analytics over the lakehouse (dashboards, saved queries, exports, data shares), and the AI platform: model registry and model risk management, deployments and monitoring, copilots with a full audit trail, and the LLM gateway policy.


### Service `regulatory-reporting-service` — database `regreport_db`

Catalogue of regulatory reports per country pack with versioned templates and data mappings; runs reports reproducibly from source snapshots, validates them, tracks manual adjustments and submits to regulators with acknowledgements. Also builds CRS and FATCA records.

### Service `analytics-service` — database `analytics_db`

Self-service analytics over whitelisted datasets: governed KPI catalogue with SQL-free metric specs, dashboards and widgets embedded in the console, saved queries in a safe query DSL, exports and scheduled data shares to the tenant's warehouse or bucket.

### Service `ai-platform-service` — database `ai_db`

Model registry with model risk management (validation, bias tests, explainability, approval), deployments in shadow/canary/champion-challenger with monitoring, feature catalogue, copilot definitions, an immutable audit of every copilot interaction, and LLM gateway policies.

## Risk, Fraud, AML and Limits (`risk`)

Real-time fraud scoring, transaction monitoring, sanctions and PEP screening, AML case management with SAR/STR filing, and the limits engine. Every payment, card authorisation and wallet movement is scored, screened and limit-checked before money moves.


### Service `fraud-service` — database `fraud_db`

Scores every authorisation, payment, wallet transfer, login and profile change in under 50 ms with rules (CEL expressions) plus ML models, maintains device intelligence and block/allow lists, raises fraud alerts and collects outcome labels for model training.

### Service `transaction-monitoring-service` — database `tm_db`

Streaming (Flink) and batch AML transaction monitoring scenarios with versioned thresholds, alerts with contributing transactions, customer AML risk rating, and an entity graph for mule and network detection.

### Service `limits-service` — database `limits_db`

Central limits engine: amount, count and balance limits by scope (tier, product, customer, account, card, wallet, agent), channel, transaction type and period; atomic check-and-reserve with commit or release, temporary overrides with approval, and risk appetite metrics.

## Servicing and CRM (`servicing`)

Customer servicing and CRM for the back-office console: service requests and cases, complaints with regulatory SLAs and redress, a unified interaction timeline across channels, notes, work queues with SLA policies, a knowledge base, and an AI copilot that summarises history and drafts responses with a full audit trail.


### Service `crm-service` — database `crm_db`

Cases, complaints, interactions, notes, work queues and SLAs for servicing staff, plus the knowledge base and the servicing copilot. Builds the customer timeline from its own records and from events of other domains.

## Treasury and ALM (`treasury`)

Front-to-back treasury: money market, FX and securities deals with confirmations and settlement, counterparty limits, liquidity positions and Basel III ratios (LCR/NSFR) with stress testing, and asset-liability management (repricing gap, NII/EVE sensitivity) with funds transfer pricing.


### Service `treasury-deal-service` — database `treasury_deal_db`

Front and middle office for treasury: counterparties and limits, money market, FX and securities deals, confirmations (MT300/MT320) and settlement instructions; posts to the ledger on settlement, accrual and maturity, and releases payment instructions through payment-service.

Interest rate risk in the banking book: repricing gap, NII and EVE sensitivity under rate shocks, behavioural assumptions, and funds transfer pricing curves and assignments.

## Wallets, Agents and Merchants (`wallets`)

Mobile money and e-wallets (the Mobiquity / Inswitch use case): customer, merchant, agent and system wallets with KYC-tier limits; agent networks with float, tills and devices; a multi-level commission engine; biller catalogue, bill payments and airtime; merchant acceptance (QR, terminals, payment links) and settlement; USSD and SMS channels; G2P and bulk disbursements; interoperability with national switches and other wallets. Every money movement posts through the ledger.


### Service `wallet-service` — database `wallet_db`

Wallet lifecycle, KYC-tier limits, PINs, linked bank accounts and every wallet money movement (P2P, cash-in/out, merchant, bill, airtime, G2P, wallet-to-bank, reversals). Each transaction is broken into legs and posted atomically to the ledger.

### Service `commission-service` — database `commission_db`

Multi-level commission engine: versioned plans with rules by transaction type, channel, tier, agent level, territory and biller; real-time accrual on every completed transaction; periodic or real-time payout runs to commission wallets with tax withholding.

### Service `biller-service` — database `biller_db`

Biller catalogue (utilities, telecom, TV, government, education), airtime and bundle products, bill inquiry and validation, bill payments and airtime top-ups with provider integration and retries, and periodic settlement to billers.

### Service `interop-service` — database `interop_db`

Interoperability with national switches, Mojaloop hubs and partner wallets/banks: participant directory, party lookup, quotes, two-phase transfers (reserve, commit, abort) with liquidity and net-debit-cap control, and inbound callbacks.
